key_insight: Geometric nonlinearity alone creates a distinct near-tip crack-opening regime and a nonlinear length scale λ_nl that grows with K_I^2, providing a baseline for nonlinear fracture in soft solids.
engineering_relevance: For soft elastic materials, this shows that large-deformation kinematics can shield the crack tip and produce apparent toughening even without material nonlinearity.
method: Model static mode-I plane-strain cracks with a compressible St. Venant-Kirchhoff solid.
Use crack-tip opening displacement (CTOD) profiles to detect deviation from linear elastic fracture mechanics.
Derive asymptotic solutions and matched-asymptotics to define the nonlinear length scale λ_nl.
evidence_signal: The paper supports its claims through analytical asymptotic derivations and CTOD-based postprocessing, showing a near-tip deviation from classical linear predictions.
watch_item: Results are for an idealized brittle, geometrically nonlinear but materially simple constitutive model, so extension to real soft materials with stronger material nonlinearity may not be direct.
paper_title: Crack-Tip Opening as a Probe for Length-Scale Separation in Geometrically Nonlinear Solids
